disease_label_per_paper: Severe adenovirus pneumonia in an immunocompetent adult
presentation_summary: Previously healthy 16-year-old male presented with one day of sudden dry cough and shortness of breath.
At emergency presentation he was febrile, tachypneic, tachycardic, normotensive, and profoundly hypoxemic on room air.
Initial chest radiograph and CT did not show parenchymal lung disease, but within hours he required ICU transfer and mechanical ventilation.

During the next 72 hours he developed worsening respiratory failure, fluid-resistant shock, bilateral consolidation and pleural effusions, conjunctival congestion, and nonoliguric acute renal failure.
Tracheal and nasopharyngeal aspirates later tested strongly positive for adenovirus by direct immunofluorescence; bacterial and multiple other infectious tests were negative.

Initial imaging was normal but later imaging showed bilateral consolidation and pleural effusion; both facts are preserved rather than collapsed into a single static pneumonia score.
The case text reports acute renal failure without a numeric creatinine value.
